appName: Google (Gmail API via Google Auth Platform)
summary: Google OAuth is fast to set up for testing — no review needed for up to 100 test users. But production access to sensitive scopes needs Google verification, and restricted scopes like Gmail additionally require a paid third-party security assessment that can take weeks and repeats annually.

decision.question: Who will connect: only people in your Google Workspace org, or anyone with a Google account?

options.name: Internal
pickWhen: Only users in your own Workspace org will connect
options.tradeoff: No verification needed, but requires a Google Workspace organization. Not usable for public apps.

options.name: External (Testing)
pickWhen: Fewer than 100 users, all added by hand
options.tradeoff: Instant, but every user must be added as a test user and sees a warning for sensitive scopes.

options.name: External (Production)
pickWhen: Any Google user should be able to connect
options.tradeoff: Requires verification for sensitive/restricted scopes or a logo; can take weeks.

decision.recommendation: Start with External in Testing mode. Decide on verification as soon as you know which scopes you need.

difficultyReason: Testing mode is fast and review-free for up to 100 users. But taking an app with sensitive scopes to production requires Google verification (about 10 business days), and restricted scopes like Gmail additionally require a paid third-party security assessment (CASA) that can take weeks and must be redone annually.

time.setup: 30-60 min to a working Testing-mode setup
time.approvalWait: None in Testing mode. For production with sensitive scopes: about 10 business days. For restricted scopes (e.g. Gmail): verification plus a paid security assessment, several weeks, repeated annually.
time.notes: Measured 42 min total in this test for project setup, Branding, Audience, client creation, fixing 3 errors, and testing two scopes. Tester had prior basic Google OAuth experience, so a first-timer may take longer. Verification and security-assessment time for production were not tested directly — see sources on the relevant claims.

accessCost.pricingModel: OAuth sign-in itself is free. Standard use of the Gmail API behind it is free within generous per-minute/per-day quotas measured in quota units, not dollars; other Google APIs behind OAuth (e.g. Maps Platform) can have their own separate paid pricing not covered by this guide.
accessCost.rates: Gmail API: no per-call dollar charge for standard use. Different methods cost different quota units (e.g. drafts.send = 100 units), capped at 1,200,000 units/minute per project and 6,000 units/minute per user.
accessCost.freeTierLimits: 1,200,000 quota units/minute per project, 6,000 units/minute per user, 80,000,000 units/day. Google has signaled usage beyond quota limits may incur Cloud billing charges later in 2026 — not confirmed whether this is already in effect.

whenReviewIsNeeded.text: No review is needed in Testing mode, whether Internal or External with up to 100 test users.

Verification is required before moving to production if the app requests sensitive or restricted scopes, has more than 10 domains, or has a logo uploaded. Uploading a logo alone triggers verification, even for an app using only basic scopes.
Sensitive-scope verification typically takes about 10 business days.

Restricted scopes (e.g. Gmail, Drive, Fit) require a paid third-party security assessment (CASA) in addition to verification — roughly $500-$4,500 depending on tier, taking 2-6+ weeks, and must be redone annually.

requirements.text: An app name and a user support email for Branding — the support email is shown to users on the consent screen.
For External Testing: a list of test users (up to 100, added by hand) who will be allowed to sign in.
The Gmail API (or whichever Google API you're calling) must be enabled on the project before it can be used.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Create a new project in the Google Cloud console — this is where the OAuth client and consent screen will live.

steps.title: Set up Branding
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform > Branding, set the app name and user support email. Don't upload a logo yet if you're still in Testing — a logo alone triggers the verification requirement.

steps.title: Choose Audience
steps.detail: Pick Internal (your Workspace org only) or External (any Google account). For External in Testing mode, add up to 100 test users by hand under Audience > Test users.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Under Clients, create a new OAuth client of type 'Web application'. Add your Authorised JavaScript origins and Authorised redirect URIs — the scheme (http vs https) must match exactly what your app sends.

steps.title: Decide on the 'AI-powered agent' client setting
steps.detail: The client page has a 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' checkbox, off by default. Google warns that changing it may affect how the app works and may not be reversible in the future — treat it as a one-way decision rather than a toggle to experiment with.

steps.title: Enable the APIs you need
steps.detail: Enable the specific Google API (e.g. Gmail API) on your project under APIs & Services > Library before making calls to it.

steps.title: Hand off the client ID and secret to Composio
steps.detail: Composio manages the authorization flow, token exchange, and refresh once it has these credentials — you don't implement any of that yourself.

blockers.fix: Make the scheme match exactly between the console (e.g. https://) and the authorization URL (e.g. http://) your app sends. Use 'error details' on the error page to see the exact URI Google received.

blockers.problem: Error 403: access_denied ("has not completed the Google verification process")
blockers.fix: The signing-in account isn't on the test user list. Go to Audience > Test users > Add users.

blockers.problem: 'Ineligible accounts not added' popup when adding a test user
blockers.fix: This popup doesn't explain the cause. Check the test user list first — the account may already be on it (in this test, the list showed the user and sign-in still worked).

blockers.problem: Uploading a logo to Branding triggers Google's verification requirement, even if your app only uses basic (non-sensitive) scopes.
blockers.fix: Skip the logo field while you're still testing. Only add one once you're ready to go through verification.

blockers.problem: The 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' checkbox on the OAuth client looks like a minor setting but its effect is unclear and Google says it may not be changeable in the future.
blockers.fix: Enabling it produced no visible change in this test, but don't flip it just to experiment — Google warns the classification may affect how the app works and that a new client may be needed if you later want to change it. Only enable it if you're confident the client is for an AI agent.

agentCanDo: Find the Google Auth Platform Branding/Audience/Clients pages and their current fields
Pre-fill the app name, support email, and redirect URIs
Check prerequisites before verification — logo specs, homepage, privacy policy URL
Draft the verification submission — scope justifications and use-case explanation for the reviewer
humanMustDo: Create the Google Cloud project and complete Branding
Choose Internal vs. External audience and, for External, add test users
Create the OAuth client and configure redirect URIs
Decide whether to mark the client as an AI-powered agent
Submit for verification and/or the CASA security assessment before going to production with sensitive/restricted scopes
